title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The previous page lists conjectural 'descriptions' (realization data) of motives over number fields: Betti–de Rham, Betti–Hodge, and so on. It then lists p-adic analogues for p-divisible groups or 'pseudo-motifs' over a complete discretely valued field K with perfect residue field of characteristic p: 3') a 'Hodge-p structure' (a Q_p-module N with a bigrading on N⊗C, i.e. a Hodge–Tate decomposition), 5') the Tate module, 6') a filtered Frobenius-crystal. It ends by asking what should replace the comparison 'double visages' 1') and 4'). This page is a computation testing such a double visage Tate–Hodge.

Set-up in modern terms.
- π = Gal(K̄/K), and C is the completion of K̄ (C_p), on which π acts.
- u: π → G(Q_p) is the p-adic Galois representation, with G the Tannakian (motivic or Tate-side) group.
- G' is the group of the 'Hodge-p' side. Its grading cocharacter is j_2: G_m → G', so j_2(Q_p^*) ⊂ G'(Q_p).
- χ: π → Q_p^* is the cyclotomic character.
- The comparison is an isomorphism α: G(C) ≅ G'(C). It plays the role of the Hodge–Tate comparison V⊗C ≅ ⊕ C(-i)^{h_i}.
- E is the canonical extension 1 → G'(C) → E → π → 1, i.e. essentially the semidirect product of G'(C) by π acting through its action on C.
- Via α, E is identified with the analogous extension of π by G(C).
- Each structure gives a splitting. σ_2 normalizes G'(Q_p), and twisting it by the Hodge–Tate cocharacter gives the splitting γ ↦ σ̃_2(γ) = σ_2(γ) j_2(χ(γ)). This encodes 'γ acts on C(i) by χ(γ)^i ⊗ γ'.
- σ_1 normalizes G(Q_p), and twisting by u gives σ̃_1(γ) = σ_1(γ) u(γ). This encodes 'γ acts on V⊗C by u(γ)⊗γ'.

The comparison axiom. The comparison is required to be Galois-equivariant: σ̃_1 = σ̃_2. Equivalently, the 'period cocycle' φ(γ) = σ_1(γ)^{-1}σ_2(γ) factors as φ(γ) = u(γ)·j_2(χ(γ))^{-1}, with u(γ) ∈ G(Q_p) and j_2(χ(γ)^{-1}) in the cocharacter torus.

Consequences drawn.
1) On Ker χ (the Galois group of K(μ_{p^∞})), u = φ. So the representation restricted to Ker χ is recovered from the comparison data, i.e. from the cocycle measuring how α fails to be Galois-invariant.
2) Ker u = {γ : χ(γ)=1, φ(γ)=1} is therefore 'known'. Then Π_1 = π/Ker u is a p-adic analytic group (Lazard) with an induced character χ_1: Π_1 → Q_p^*.
The page breaks off here.

Purpose. The aim is to test whether a 'Tate–Hodge double visage' (Galois representation plus Hodge–Tate group with cocharacter, compared over C_p) carries enough information to replace the missing comparison realizations. It is an early, group-theoretic formulation of Hodge–Tate comparison as an equality of two semilinear splittings, i.e. a torsor or period-cocycle formulation.
errors: The equality Ker u = {χ=1, φ=1} needs Ker u ⊂ Ker χ, i.e. that the cyclotomic character factors through u. This holds if G contains the weight/Tate-twist information (Q_p(1) lies in the Tannakian category, so G → G_m with χ = (that map)∘u). It is not automatic; otherwise one only gets {χ=1, φ=1} ⊂ Ker u.

The statement 'u known on Ker χ' is somewhat tautological. φ is built from the splittings, which already encode u through the comparison α. The real content is that, given the comparison torsor, Galois action and Hodge–Tate cocharacter determine each other up to χ.
j_2 lives in G' while u lives in G. The product u(γ)·j_2(χ(γ)^{-1}) silently uses α to transport j_2 into G(C).

ideas.what: Hodge–Tate decomposition of a p-adic Galois representation viewed as a 'Hodge-p structure' (Q_p-space with grading over C_p) to be compared with the Tate module
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (1967, p-divisible groups); later Fontaine, Faltings
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Grothendieck's 1970 ICM talk on Barsotti–Tate groups ('mysterious functor'); unsure

ideas.what: Encoding a semilinear comparison as two splittings of the extension G(C)⋊π and their discrepancy cocycle φ = σ_1^{-1}σ_2 = u·j_2(χ)^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Period torsor / comparison cocycle; Galois action on the C_p-points of the Hodge–Tate cocharacter
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fontaine (period rings and admissibility, 1979–82); Serre 'Groupes algébriques associés aux modules de Hodge–Tate' (1979)

ideas.what: Relating the Galois image to the Hodge–Tate cocharacter and cyclotomic character (the Galois image restricted to Ker χ is controlled by the comparison; the image is a p-adic analytic group)
ideas.modern_name: Sen theory / Hodge–Tate cocharacter in the Zariski closure of the Galois image (Sen 1973, Serre 1979); Lazard p-adic Lie groups

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a p-adic 'Tate–Hodge double visage': Tannakian groups G (Tate side) and G' (Hodge–Tate side with cocharacter j_2), compared over C_p, with Galois-compatibility written as equality of twisted splittings. He starts deducing structural information on the Galois image from it (u on Ker χ, Ker u, Π_1 p-adic analytic). This anticipates the group-theoretic Hodge–Tate analysis of Sen and Serre (1973/1979) and Fontaine's period formalism. The thread breaks off.
missed.quote: On écrit que σ̃_1(γ)=σ̃_2(γ) ... φ(γ) = u(γ).j_2(χ(γ^{-1})) ... Π_1=π/Ker u ... un groupe analytique p-adique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical evidence that Grothendieck (c.1969–72) was formulating p-adic comparison as a Tannakian / torsor compatibility of two semilinear structures. It predates or parallels Sen–Serre–Fontaine. It is relevant to the history of the 'mysterious functor' and of p-adic Mumford–Tate groups.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early, unpublished Tannakian formulation of a Hodge–Tate comparison as equality of two splittings of a semilinear extension, with first consequences for the Galois image. That is historically interesting, as it anticipates Sen/Serre/Fontaine ideas. But the computation is elementary, partly tautological, incomplete, and the eventual theory is well developed in the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'se factorise' is plausibly 'normalise ... et se factorise par' or 'est fixé par'; uncertain.
'induit par p' at the end is probably 'induit par χ' (χ_1 induced by χ).
The final line is likely 'est un groupe analytique p-adique, et ...' referring to Π_1.
In the diagram, the top arrow is u: π → G(Q_p), and α: G(C) ≅ G'(C) is the vertical identification.
